package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner;

import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.repository.OwnerRepository;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto.OwnerFieldsDto;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation.DuplicateOwnerTelephoneException;

/**
 * Rejects a create body whose normalized telephone is already held by another owner,
 * so the endpoint responds 409. Runs after {@link NormalizeOwnerTelephone} so the
 * comparison uses the bare 10-digit value.
 */
public class RejectDuplicateOwnerTelephone {

    public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, OwnerRepository ownerRepository)
            throws DuplicateOwnerTelephoneException {
        String telephone = request.getTelephone();
        for (Owner existing : ownerRepository.findAll()) {
            if (telephone.equals(existing.getTelephone())) {
                throw new DuplicateOwnerTelephoneException(telephone);
            }
        }
    }
}

## What I did

Added email uniqueness enforcement as a new, self-contained pipeline step — mirroring the existing telephone-duplicate rule, so no existing function grew.

**New files (each a small, cohesive unit with zero surrounding class complexity):**
- `RejectDuplicateOwnerEmail.java` — one `service` method: skips absent/blank emails, else scans owners and throws `DuplicateOwnerEmailException` when a lower-cased email collides.
- `DuplicateOwnerEmailException.java` — checked exception (so it appears in `throws`).
- `DuplicateOwnerEmailExceptionHandler.java` — responds `409 CONFLICT`.
- `DuplicateOwnerEmailException.yml` escalation mapping.

**One-line wiring change:**
- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted `rejectDuplicateEmail` right after `normalizeEmail`, so the comparison uses the already-lower-cased value.

**Structural-impact note:** I placed the logic after `NormalizeOwnerEmail` (which already lower-cases the request email) rather than editing that class, so no existing function's body or complexity changed. The one edited file (the YAML) touches only a low-complexity, declarative step list. All new behaviour lives in fresh classes with `WMC_other ≈ 0`.
